_note: Worked example concepts for recall_extender.py --concepts (post-submission addition, 2026-07-23), paired with ./corpus.json. 3 specialist terms from the LHC/collider micro-black-hole safety case (see demo-collider/README.md), each owned by one of the two communities in corpus.json. 'constrained_definition' for all three is HAND-AUTHORED by the person building this example (not generated by an LLM, not copied from demo-collider/term-check/'s own model-generated restatements) -- written directly from the primary excerpts in corpus.json, following the same hard constraints as llm_backend.py's DEFINE_PROMPT (no use of the term itself, no proper names, no field name). This mirrors how the original 3 eggs concepts in ../concepts.json were built (author-frozen, not live-generated) -- see ../README.md's stage-2 honesty note. Running this file through recall_extender.py IS a scored run (every concept has 'owning_community') but is still a DEMONSTRATION, not an independent measurement: the corpus is small (13 docs), hand-selected by the same person who wrote the definitions, and the owning-community label was never checked against an outside judge -- it is read directly off the source papers' own section structure (see corpus.json's 'source' fields).

concepts.naive_question: could a black hole made at a particle collider end up swallowing the Earth
concepts.constrained_definition: A reduction in a moving compact object's speed that happens specifically because the object is capturing nearby matter into itself as it travels, gaining mass in the process, as distinct from slowing that comes only from gravitationally deflecting nearby matter without taking any of it in.

concepts.naive_question: could a black hole made at a particle collider end up swallowing the Earth
concepts.constrained_definition: A regime describing how a small, localized body that pulls in nearby matter interacts with the material around it: when its range of influence is smaller than the typical spacing between the individual particles making up that matter, it takes them in one at a time as separate objects; when its range of influence is larger than that spacing, the surrounding matter behaves instead like one smooth, continuous substance.

concepts.naive_question: could a black hole made at a particle collider end up swallowing the Earth
concepts.constrained_definition: The time for a body undergoing repeated random redirection by nearby matter -- traveling only as fast as a limited average distance between redirections allows, with a steady pull adding a net drift on top of that random motion -- to work its way completely through an outer bounding layer of material, estimated from the slowest-moving point within that layer.
